title: Dynamic behavior based churn prediction in mobile telecom
harvard_reference: Alboukaey, N., Joukhadar, A. and Ghneim, N. (2020) 'Dynamic behavior based churn prediction in mobile telecom', Expert Systems with Applications, 162, 113779. doi:10.1016/j.eswa.2020.113779.
abstract_summary: Argues that monthly, static behavioural features miss day-to-day changes before churn and flag early-month leavers too late. It models each customer's daily behaviour as a multivariate time series and compares four daily models: RFM-based and statistics-based models on extracted features, and LSTM and CNN models that learn features. On 150 days of data from an MTN mobile operator, daily models beat monthly ones, predicting churners earlier and more accurately. LSTM beats CNN, but LSTM and CNN only equal the RFM-based model; all three beat the statistics-based model.

claims_supported.claim: Sequence (LSTM, CNN) churn models need daily usage series and, even then, only matched an RFM-feature model.
claims_supported.where: Abstract (publisher abstract via the Semantic Scholar API): daily behaviour modelled as multivariate time series; daily models beat monthly ones; LSTM and CNN performed equal to the RFM-based model. Full text not read.
